tutorial.title: Creating Variables
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to create variables in Python.

lessons.title: Python 1
lessons.interactiveContent: Python is a fantastic programming language for beginners and experts alike.

lessons.title: Python 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
It's the language of choice for many companies and a popular pick for personal projects.

You can use it for automating tasks, getting ahead in work with data analysis, machine learning, and much more!

lessons.title: Moving boxes
lessons.interactiveContent:
No matter how complex a program is, it begins with a single line of code. This first line is usually a variable.

Programs use variables to remember information. Like moving boxes, variables have content and names that tell us what's inside.

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do computers use variables for?

To store information for later useTo display information on the screen

To store information for later use.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A program shows a player's name in three different places. Why put the name in a variable first?

Store it once, reuse it everywhere it's neededShow it on the screen automaticallyIt makes the program run faster

Store it once, reuse it everywhere it's needed.

lessons.title: Creating a name with no spaces
lessons.interactiveContent:
To create a variable, we start by typing its name. Variable names need to be single words and, therefore, have no spaces.

Tap on the word city to start creating the variable.

Make sure to pick city.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To create a variable, we start by typing its name. Variable names need to be single words and, therefore, have no spaces.

Create the variable by picking a valid name for the city.

Make sure to pick city.

lessons.title: Snake case
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want a variable name with multiple words, we use snake case. Snake case means using _ to connect the additional words.

Make sure to pick _.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we want a variable name with multiple words, we use snake case. Snake case means using _ to connect the additional words.

Connect all three words into one snake case variable name.

Make sure to pick _, followed by _.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this variable name?

There's a space between the wordsIt contains a lowercase letter

There's a space between the words.
lessons.hardModeContent:
This variable name breaks a rule. Which one?

A name can't contain a space, so it must be a single wordA name must be more descriptive than thisThe words need a capital letter to join them, like highScore

A name can't contain a space, so it must be a single word.

lessons.title: Descriptive names
lessons.interactiveContent:
To help us understand what's inside a variable we pick descriptive names.

Make sure to pick home_city_province.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To help us understand what's inside a variable we pick descriptive names.

Pick the name that is descriptive and written in snake case.

Make sure to pick home_city_province.

lessons.title: Example 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pick the most descriptive variable name.

Make sure to pick high_score.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pick the most descriptive variable name written in snake case.

Make sure to pick high_score.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does snake case format multiple words when creating a variable name?

Using underscores (e.g., my_variable_name)Using capital letters (e.g., myVariableName)

Using underscores (e.g., my_variable_name).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which variable name is written in snake case?

total_cash_amountTotalCashAmounttotal-cash-amount

Make sure to pick total_cash_amount.

lessons.title: Question 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we give variables descriptive names like city or population instead of c or p?

To help us understand what's inside themTo make them faster to type

To help us understand what's inside them.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A teammate renames the variable t to ticket_price. What does the program gain?

Anyone reading the code can tell what the value meansThe program runs the same steps in less timeIt removes an error that a one-letter name like t would cause

Anyone reading the code can tell what the value means.

lessons.title: Example 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the right symbols to create the snake case variable.

Make sure to pick _, followed by _.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the right symbols to turn these three words into one valid variable name.

Make sure to pick _, followed by _.

lessons.title: Example 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a variable called friend_request.

Make sure to pick friend, followed by _, and finally request.

lessons.title: Different Values
lessons.interactiveContent:
Variables can contain all types of values. Let's take a look at storing text values, like "Porsche" here.

Make sure to pick "Porsche".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Variables can contain all types of values, including text.

Store the text value Porsche in the variable car_1. Text values are enclosed in quotes.

Make sure to pick "Porsche".

lessons.title: Giving a variable a value
lessons.interactiveContent:
After creating and naming a variable, we use the = sign to store a value inside it.

Type = to store the value "Miami" inside the city variable.

Make sure to type =.

lessons.title: Storing
lessons.interactiveContent:
Storing a value in a variable is like putting stuff inside a labeled box. Here, the variable device_type stores the value "apple".

Make sure to pick =, followed by "apple".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Storing a value in a variable is like putting stuff inside a labeled box. Here, the variable device_type stores the value "apple".

Make sure to pick device_type, followed by =, and finally "apple".

lessons.title: String
lessons.interactiveContent:
The values we've been storing, like "Miami" are strings. String values are text between double quotes.

Make sure to pick ", followed by ".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The values we've been storing, like "Miami" are strings. String values are text between double quotes.

Add the sign that stores the value, then wrap Miami in double quotes so it becomes a string.

Make sure to pick =, followed by ", and finally ".

lessons.title: Sentence
lessons.interactiveContent:
Strings can contain all sorts of letters and symbols, including spaces, like the value "Winter is coming.".

Make sure to pick ", followed by Winter is coming., and finally ".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Strings can contain all sorts of letters and symbols, including spaces, like the value "Winter is coming.".

Store Winter is coming. using double quotes.

Make sure to pick ", followed by Winter is coming., and finally ".

What's the value of this variable?

"Karin"name

Make sure to pick "Karin".
lessons.hardModeContent:
This line runs. Which of these is the value stored in name?

Make sure to pick "Karin".

How do we know a value is a string?

It's a text between double quotes, like "Amy"It contains the = sign

It's a text between double quotes, like "Amy".

The text "Hey Ya!" is stored under the name song_nameHey Ya! appears in the consolesong_name is stored inside "Hey Ya!"

The text "Hey Ya!" is stored under the name song_name.

hobby"Tree shaping"

Make sure to pick hobby.
lessons.hardModeContent:

hobbyhobby = "Tree shaping""Tree shaping"

lessons.title: Lines of code
lessons.interactiveContent:
Lines of code are instructions for the computer to follow.

When we run code, we tell the computer to follow the instructions we put together.

lessons.title: Order
lessons.interactiveContent:
The order of the instructions matters because the computer follows the instructions line by line.

Add the lines of code in the correct order, beginning with step_1, followed by step_2, and finally step_3.

Make sure to pick step_1 = "Collect pants", followed by step_2 = "?", and finally step_3 = "Profit".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The order of the instructions matters because the computer follows the instructions line by line.

Put the three steps in running order, from step_1 to step_3, so the computer reaches them from first to last.

Make sure to pick step_1 = "Collect pants", followed by step_2 = "?", and finally step_3 = "Profit".

lessons.title: Console
lessons.interactiveContent:
With the special instruction print(), we tell the computer to display a value in an area called the console, also known as the shell.

Make sure to pick "Hello, World!".
lessons.hardModeContent:
With the special instruction print(), we tell the computer to display a value in an area called the console, also known as the shell.

Fill the gap so the console displays Hello, World!

Make sure to pick "Hello, World!".

lessons.title: Displaying multiple times
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use the print() instruction as often as we want. The computer displays every value on a new line in the console.

Make sure to pick print, followed by (, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use the print() instruction as often as we want. The computer displays every value on a new line in the console.

Add a second line that displays GO! on its own line below.

Make sure to pick print, followed by (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Displaying variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use print() to display variables like greeting, too.

Make sure to pick greeting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use print() to display variables like greeting, too.

Print the variable so the console shows what it holds.

Make sure to pick greeting.

lessons.title: Output
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we display variables in the console, their values appear instead of their names. If we print name here, it'll show its value.

Make sure to pick name.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we display variables in the console, their values appear instead of their names. If we print name here, it'll show its value.

Use the variable name inside print() so the console shows what it holds.

Make sure to pick name.

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we know "Hello, World!" is a string?

It starts and ends with double quotesIt contains letters and symbols

It starts and ends with double quotes.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You display "Hello, World!" with print(). Why does the code need the quotes?

They mark the value as a stringThey make quote marks appear in the consoleThey create a variable named Hello, World!

They mark the value as a string.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the console?

An area that displays outputThe area where we write the code

An area that displays output.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your code runs print("Hi!"). Where does Hi! show up?

In the console, the area that displays outputIn the code area, right below the line that printed itIn a pop-up window on your screen

In the console, the area that displays output.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the special instruction print() do?

It displays a value in the consoleIt creates a variable

It displays a value in the console.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A program creates values but never uses print(). What shows up in the console?

Nothing, because values only appear when printedEvery value, as soon as it is createdOnly the last value, shown automatically at the end

Nothing, because values only appear when printed.
